text: Hello and welcome to Force Be [music]
Tim Coaching. My name is Blake Townend.
Week two brings us to Oulton Park
International. This lap time was done on
my sixth lap [music] in this stint.
Brake bias was set to 54%. B lap and O
lap are posted in my Discord server,
which is pinned below in the comments.
>> [music]
>> Approaching turn one, brake before the
black banner on the left. Peak at 60%
brake pressure and trail towards the
apex. Third gear, get back to power
before you strike the curb.
Turn three [music] is downhill. We're
braking at the beginning of the inverted
hump. Brake at roughly 55% pressure and
in third gear. Get back to full throttle
once you feel the car squat down. Nibble
the apex curb, but don't be greedy.
Don't forget to like, sub, and click on
that bell icon. Thank you.
For turn four, I lifted off the throttle
to allow the front end to gain traction.
However, it's better to use a small
amount brake pressure to accomplish
faster rotation. Get close to the curb.
Entering turn five, there's a dirt patch
on the left. Use that as your braking
point. Use threshold braking and then
trail into the corner. Be in second
gear. Keep the car low and back to full
throttle once the front tires grip.
For turn six, glance to your right and
brake before the marshal stand. Use 60%
brake pressure and use second gear. I
like to get close to the tire bundles as
possible to maximize speed.
Turn 10. Brake at the 100 meter board. I
peak at 70-ish percent and into second
gear. Use as much curb as possible for
both corners. Don't track out too wide
after turn 11 as we need to open up the
entry for turn 12. Briefly use medium
and throttle [music] and keep the car
into second gear. Hit the inside curb of
turn 12, but don't be greedy. The car
will become unsettled and delay
traction. Don't run too wide on exit to
the point that you bottom out.
Approaching turn 15, use the green and
white stripes at the end of the tire
barrier on the right as your braking
point. Down shift into third. Get as
close as possible to the curbs to make a
double apex. Another exit that can catch
you well if you run too wide.
Your braking point for the last corner
is actually after you go over the crest.
I peak at 85% brake pressure and into
second gear. Back the power as soon as
your car is alongside the start of the
curb. Keep the car to the left to
shorten track distance. [music]
That was a 1 minute 43.954.
>> Woo!
